subject: Runway rediscovery — prioritized escrow & close re-anchor request
messages:
From: Diane Chen <diane.chen@orionhealthtech.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Luke Porter <luke.porter@orionhealthtech.com>, Procurement <procurement@orionhealthtech.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial MAP check-in — timeline pressure starting this sprint

Hi Camila,

Quick note from our side — we ran the org-level review this morning and surfaced a capacity shortage across two integration teams. That pushes our internal evals out by ~2 weeks if we remain on current scope.

We still want to hit the H2 go-live target, but the PMs asked whether Redwood can propose a reprofile that preserves the primary acceptance window. Specifically: can you quantify the minimum acceptance slice (subset of features + test matrix) that would keep the first customer pilot on track? We need this so we can present a pragmatic MAP to our execs.

Also, procurement will need a clear statement on credits/fallbacks if we miss the agreed final milestone — they flagged the absence of any escrow/credit language. Luke looped them in.

Can you share a short counter-proposal (MAP rebaseline + prioritized acceptance) and indicate any credit/escrow options your side can accept?

Thanks — Diane
Diane Chen
Head of Platform Integrations | Orion HealthTech

---
Attachments: (none in this message)
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Diane Chen <diane.chen@orionhealthtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP check-in — timeline pressure starting this sprint

Hi Diane — thanks for the heads-up and for being transparent. We appreciate wanting to preserve H2.

Quick summary of what I can commit to now (high-level):
- Prioritized acceptance slice: we can carve out a pilot scope with the core inference pipeline + embeddings-only search and a reduced test matrix that covers the top 3 customer workflows. That reduces end-to-end acceptance scope by ~40%. Estimated impact: trims customer-facing validation by 10–14 days.
- MAP rebaseline: attached is a draft MAP (Orion_MAP_v2.xlsx) that shows a 10-business-day reprofile, plus a 14-day contingency lane if integration bandwidth slips further.
- Escrow / credits: we don't offer full-custody escrow, but we can agree to a two-part commercial backstop: (a) a 10% credit on the first paid month if final sign-off is delayed beyond the contingency lane, or (b) a technical canary deployment at reduced throughput (no charge for N tokens/day) to preserve pilot continuity while integration completes. We included proposed clause language in procurement_clause_redline.docx.

Notes / asks from your side to make the MAP actionable:
1) Confirm the prioritized feature list (I annotated the MAP with a recommended slice; need your PMs to sign it).
2) Confirm which tests are non-negotiable for your security/compliance gate (SOC2 artifacts will be separate).
3) Procurement: confirm whether a one-off credit or a canary deployment is preferable. We can finalize language either way.

I'll schedule a short call to walk the MAP and trade-offs with Luke and your PMs — Est. 30 minutes. Proposed times: Wed 14th 11:00–11:30 or Thu 15th 09:00–09:30 PT.

Camila Reyes
Solutions Director, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0131
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Orion_MAP_v2.xlsx, procurement_clause_redline.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Diane Chen <diane.chen@orionhealthtech.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@orionhealthtech.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP check-in — timeline pressure starting this sprint

Diane / Luke — looping in a brief commercial proposal to avoid repeated rework and to give your execs a predictable mitigation path.

We propose the following prioritized-escrow hybrid (short form):
- If Orion confirms the prioritized acceptance slice within 3 business days, Redwood will commit to the 10-business-day reprofile and stand up a zero-cost canary (up to 50k inference tokens/day) for a max of 21 days following the original final milestone date.
- If the final acceptance slips beyond the 21-day canary, Redwood will apply a 10% invoice credit to the first month following sign-off.
- If Redwood-triggered regression is demonstrated in production (rare), we will provide a one-time 15% credit in lieu of additional engineering hours related to the regression.

Operational asks:
- Camila: confirm that the MAP in Orion_MAP_v2.xlsx reflects the minimal test matrix and that the security gate items are annotated.
- Diane/Luke: confirm procurement preference (canary vs invoice credit) so we can insert the final wording into DocuSign.

I know credits are sensitive — this is structured to prioritize continuity (canary) and keep total commercial exposure modest. If procurement would rather have a holdback/escrow deposit, we can model that, but it will require a short SLA amendment.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: SLA_Primer.pdf
From: Luke Porter <luke.porter@orionhealthtech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Diane Chen <diane.chen@orionhealthtech.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@orionhealthtech.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP check-in — timeline pressure starting this sprint

Thanks — all. Quick confirmation from procurement: canary first, credit second. The pilot PMs also accepted Camila's minimal-slice annotations with two small edits (added regression test A.2 and an additional auth smoke test).

Next steps we agreed on the call:
- Orion to update the MAP sheet with the two edits by EOD tomorrow.
- Redwood to finalize the canary configuration and DocuSign clause (we prefer the canary to be live a week before original go-live to validate traffic patterns).
- Procurement requests a 1-page commercial summary (we can attach as an addendum to the PO) — can Marissa own that?

Luke Porter
Director, Program Delivery | Orion HealthTech
